data.content:
Here are the top pairs of substances with the highest co-driver frequency (via the JOINT_DRIVER_WITH relationship), along with how often both substances are detected (median_concentration > 0) at the same sites:

| Substance 1      | Substance 2                  | Joint Driver Frequency | Co-Detection Count |
|------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| Methoxychlor     | Terbutylazine               | 53                    | 14                 |
| Cyanuric acid    | Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene      | 48                    | 17                 |
| Endrin           | Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene      | 47                    | 79                 |
| Carbendazim      | Imidacloprid                | 44                    | 1298               |
| Carbofuran       | Metazachlor                 | 44                    | 157                |

Summary of findings:
- The pairs with the highest co-driver frequency do not always have the highest co-detection counts. For example, Carbendazim and Imidacloprid are detected together at 1298 sites, while Methoxychlor and Terbutylazine, despite having the highest joint driver frequency, are co-detected at only 14 sites.
- Some pairs (e.g., Endrin and Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene) have moderate co-detection counts (79 sites), while others (e.g., Cyanuric acid and Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene) are co-detected less frequently (17 sites).

This suggests that while certain substance pairs frequently act as joint risk drivers, they do not always tend to be detected together at the same sites. There is variability in co-detection frequency among the top joint driver pairs.

You can access the full Neo4j graph database and run the provided Cypher query for more details at: https://zenodo.org/records/14616124

Cypher query used:
```cypher
// Step 1: Find top pairs of substances with highest JOINT_DRIVER_WITH frequency
MATCH (s1:Substance)-[j:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]->(s2:Substance)
WITH s1, s2, j.frequency AS joint_driver_frequency
ORDER BY joint_driver_frequency DESC
LIMIT 20

// Step 2: For each pair, count sites where both are detected (median_concentration > 0)
MATCH (s1)-[r1:MEASURED_AT]->(site:Site)<-[r2:MEASURED_AT]-(s2)
WHERE r1.median_concentration > 0 AND r2.median_concentration > 0
WITH s1.Name AS Substance1, s2.Name AS Substance2, joint_driver_frequency,
     count(DISTINCT site) AS CoDetectionCount

RETURN Substance1, Substance2, joint_driver_frequency AS JointDriverFrequency, 
       CoDetectionCount
ORDER BY JointDriverFrequency DESC, CoDetectionCount DESC
```
